verification_report.summary: The proof is correct. Reduction preserves the required analytic hypotheses and the full CLD form calculus; the finite lifted-chart argument also proves the necessary homeomorphism on compact test forms, so currents, weak topologies, positivity, closedness, permitted products, psh functions, and G-forms are transported correctly. The integration current changes exactly by the generic multiplicities in the fundamental cycle, while the reduced curve-rigidity theorem gives the claimed unique componentwise classification. For the Bedford--Taylor assertion, the weighted and unweighted curvature equalities both force the normalization-component curvature differences to be supported over the locally finite type-1 conductor/intersection locus; the zero-atom lemma then makes every component difference vanish, yielding the exact equivalence and the conclusion for every positive closed current. All cited CLD25 statements were checked against the official arXiv v2 source and apply with matching definitions and hypotheses.
